results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** The finite-second-moment inputs, independent Gaussian noises, and average power bounds in the statement; entropy is measured in bits.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the Gaussian and information suppliers.

[F1] [[def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel]]: the channel, SNR/INR convention, and average input power constraints.

[F2] [[lem-complex-scalar-gaussian-maximum-differential-entropy]]: a complex variable of variance $v$ has entropy at most $\log_2(\pi e v)$.

[F3] [[lem-bounded-density-finite-second-moment-has-finite-differential-entropy]]: bounded densities of finite second moment have finite differential entropy.

[F4] [[lem-standard-borel-conditional-mutual-information-chain-rule-and-data-processing]]: conditional mutual-information chain rules, nonnegativity, and data processing.

[F5] [[lem-scalar-gaussian-channel-mutual-information-power-bound]]: the Gaussian-noise density identity and scalar power bound, with equality for circular Gaussian inputs.



1.1 If $(T,S)$ are Gaussian-smoothed finite-second-moment variables, then $h(T|S)=h(T-kS|S)\le h(T-kS)\le\log_2(\pi e\operatorname{Var}(T-kS))$ for every complex $k$. The first identity is conditional translation and the first inequality is conditional mutual-information nonnegativity; the second is [F2]. A finite-dimensional convolution with a nonsingular Gaussian has a density bounded by the peak of that Gaussian and finite second moment; [F3], applied after identifying complex vectors with real vectors, therefore makes every relevant joint, marginal, and residual differential entropy finite. In particular the pairs $(Y_1^n,S_1^n)$ and $(Y_2^n,S_2^n)$ have nonsingular independent receiver-noise coordinates, and the degraded pair below has nonsingular joint Gaussian noise when $s>t$. Their conditional entropies are differences of these finite joint and marginal entropies. For conditioning additionally on $X_1^n$, which need not have a density, first subtract its known translated contribution; independence removes that conditioning and leaves the nonsingular smoothed pair $(h_{22}X_2^n+Z_2^n,S_2^n)$. The information-density identity, obtained by integrating the Gaussian conditional density divided by the output density as in [F5], then justifies the remaining conditional entropy identities without infinite subtractions. At zero signal power the same Gaussian density argument applies without alteration. Coordinate entropy chain rules give $h(T^n|S^n)\le\sum_j h(T_j|S_j)$. [A1, F2, F3, F4, F5, given, algebra]

2.1 Suppose $s>t$ and set $U^n=\sqrt{s}X^n+Z^n$, $V^n=\sqrt{t/s}\,U^n+\sqrt{1-t/s}\,W^n$. The marginal law of $V^n$ is the lower-SNR channel and $X^n-U^n-V^n$ is Markov. Thus the difference of the two output entropies equals $I(X^n;U^n|V^n)=h(U^n|V^n)-n\log_2(\pi e[1-t/s])$: the conditional noise is $Z^n$ given $\sqrt{t/s}Z^n+\sqrt{1-t/s}W^n$. For a coordinate variance $p_j$, minimizing the quadratic residual variance of $U_j$ given $V_j$ gives $(1-t/s)(1+sp_j)/(1+tp_j)$. Step 1.1 therefore bounds the entropy difference by $\sum_j\log_2((1+sp_j)/(1+tp_j))$. This logarithmic ratio has derivative $(s-t)/((1+sp)(1+tp)\ln2)$, which is nonnegative and decreasing. Jensen and the average variance bound yield the first claimed inequality. If $s=t$ the two marginal entropies agree; if $t=0<s$ the same construction and computation apply. If $s=t=0$ both outputs are pure Gaussian noise. [F4, F5, step 1.1, given, construct, algebra, cases]

2.2 Let $p_{i,j}=\operatorname{Var}(X_{i,j})$. The optimal scalar linear estimate of $Y_{1,j}$ from $S_{1,j}$ has residual variance $1+|h_{21}|^2p_{2,j}+|h_{11}|^2p_{1,j}/(1+|h_{12}|^2p_{1,j})$: independence of the two user vectors and the noises eliminates all other covariances. Step 1.1 bounds the conditional entropy by the logarithm of this variance times $\pi e$. The map $x\mapsto x/(1+kx)$ is increasing and concave on $[0,\infty)$ for $k\ge0$, with second derivative $-2k/(1+kx)^3$; hence the residual variance is increasing and concave in the two powers, and its logarithm is also concave and increasing. Jensen and $n^{-1}\sum_jp_{i,j}\le P_i$ give the first conditional-output bound. Reflection gives the second. This calculation has no division by a channel gain and remains valid when any gain vanishes. [F1, F2, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 The output variances are $1+|h_{11}|^2p_{1,j}+|h_{21}|^2p_{2,j}$ and $1+|h_{12}|^2p_{1,j}+|h_{22}|^2p_{2,j}$. Applying the coordinate chain rule, [F2], and logarithmic Jensen gives the two unconditioned-output bounds. Given $X_1^n$, subtract its contribution from $Y_2^n$; independence leaves the linear-estimation problem for $h_{22}X_2^n+Z_2^n$ from $h_{21}X_2^n+Z_1^n$. Its coordinate residual variance is $1+|h_{22}|^2p_{2,j}/(1+|h_{21}|^2p_{2,j})$. The same concavity calculation proves the final conditional bound. Reflection proves its counterpart. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.2, given, algebra] ∎

**Given:** A complex channel, a nominal split, and a nonnegative rate pair satisfying the seven displayed facets.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the Gaussian-law and information suppliers.

[F1] [[def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel]]: the channel and its expected average power constraints.

[F2] [[cor-iid-finite-variance-weak-law]]: IID finite-variance information-density averages converge in probability to their means.

[F3] [[lem-scalar-gaussian-channel-mutual-information-power-bound]]: Gaussian scalar mutual informations have their variance-ratio values.

[F4] [[lem-standard-borel-conditional-mutual-information-chain-rule-and-data-processing]]: conditional chain rules, data processing, and nonnegativity.



1.1 For private rates $p_i\ge0$ and common rates $u_i\ge0$ with $p_i+u_i=r_i$, generate independent Gaussian common codewords $U_i(m_{ic})$ of power $P_{ic}$ and, for every common index, an independent Gaussian satellite codebook $V_i(m_{ic},m_{ip})$ of power $P_{ip}$. Transmit $U_i+V_i$. Receiver 1 uniquely decodes $(m_{1c},m_{1p})$ if some index $m_{2c}$ passes its conditional Gaussian information-density tests; it does not output $m_{2c}$. Its four false-own-message classes have rate exponents $p_1$, $r_1$, $p_1+u_2$, and $r_1+u_2$: respectively wrong private only, wrong own common and its satellite, wrong private and unintended common, and wrong own common and unintended common. Conditional on the correctly indexed layers, a false class has the product law against which its likelihood ratio has mean one. Markov's inequality at a threshold strictly between its rate exponent and its Gaussian mutual information, followed by the union bound, makes its error probability vanish if $p_1<A_1$, $r_1<D_1$, $p_1+u_2<E_1$, $r_1+u_2<G_1$. A wrong unintended index alone is not an error because it leaves the decoded own message unchanged. The true information densities are IID quadratic Gaussian functions with finite variance, so [F2] proves correct-message acceptance; [F3] gives exactly the four displayed Gaussian quantities. Receiver 2 gives $p_2<A_2$, $r_2<D_2$, $p_2+u_1<E_2$, $r_2+u_1<G_2$. Zero-rate or zero-power layers have singleton message sets and no false-message class. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Deterministic power selection is included as follows. Initially reduce every positive component power by a factor $1-\varepsilon$, with $0<\varepsilon<1$. For user $i$ let $B_{i,j}$ be its input energy at coordinate $j$, averaged over the finitely many independent message indices of that user's codebook, including the cross term in $|U_i+V_i|^2$. Across coordinates the $B_{i,j}$ are IID; Jensen gives $\mathbb E B_{i,j}^2\le\mathbb E|U_i+V_i|^4=2((1-\varepsilon)P_i)^2$, independently of message-set size. Thus $\operatorname{Var}(n^{-1}\sum_j B_{i,j})\le2P_i^2/n$ and its mean is $(1-\varepsilon)P_i$. Chebyshev makes the probability of either power exceeding $P_i$ tend to zero. The ensemble average sum of receiver errors tends to zero by step 1.1; Markov makes the probability of an error larger than the square root of that average tend to zero. Hence some deterministic codebook simultaneously meets both exact average power constraints and has vanishing errors. If a user's total power is zero, its codeword is zero and its rate is zero. Fix $\varepsilon$ first, take the coding limit, and then let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$; continuity and closure give the claimed nonslack region. This argument also applies to every simpler Gaussian codebook used below. [F1, F2, step 1.1, given, choose, algebra]

3.1 The eight inequalities in step 1.1, with closure removing strictness, project exactly to the seven stated facets plus $r_1\le A_1+E_2$ and $r_2\le A_2+E_1$. Here is an explicit elimination. Set $S=r_1+r_2$, $l_1=\max(0,S-G_2)$, $l_2=\max(0,S-G_1)$, $v_1=\min(A_1,r_1)$, $v_2=\min(A_2,r_2)$. The private rates must lie in $[l_i,v_i]$ and satisfy $r_1-E_2\le p_1-p_2\le E_1-r_2$. Such rates exist exactly when $l_i\le v_i$ and the intervals $[l_1-v_2,v_1-l_2]$ and $[r_1-E_2,E_1-r_2]$ intersect. Expanding the max/min comparisons gives $S\le A_1+G_2$, $S\le A_2+G_1$, $r_1\le A_1+E_2$, $r_2\le A_2+E_1$, $S\le E_1+E_2$, $2r_1+r_2\le A_1+G_1+E_2$, $r_1+2r_2\le A_2+G_2+E_1$, together with $r_i\le D_i$. The other comparisons are redundant: $r_i\le G_i$ follows from $D_i\le G_i$, and $S\le G_2+E_1$ or $S\le G_1+E_2$ follows from $S\le E_1+E_2$ and $E_i\le G_i$; the remaining inequalities are nonnegativity of the Gaussian mutual informations. Conversely these same comparisons ensure the intervals intersect, providing the desired $p_i$. [F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, given, algebra]

4.1 Suppose $r_1>A_1+E_2$. The seven facets give $r_2<G_2-E_2$ from $S\le A_1+G_2$, $r_2<E_1-A_1$ from $S\le E_1+E_2$, $S<G_1$ from $2r_1+r_2\le A_1+G_1+E_2$, and $r_1\le D_1$. Use a single Gaussian user 1 codebook of full power $P_1$ and only the nominal common user 2 power $P_{2c}$, carrying all of user 2's information; set its private layer to zero. At receiver 1 the MAC own-message bound is at least $D_1$, its user 2 bound is at least $E_1-A_1=I(U_2;Y_1|U_1)$, and its sum bound is at least $G_1$: removing the independent private user 2 signal only reduces noise, and conditioning additionally on the entire $X_1$ increases the user 2 bound. Receiver 2's Gaussian treating-user-1-as-noise bound is at least $G_2-E_2=I(U_2;Y_2)$ computed under the nominal law, because the private user 2 satellite has been removed. These four inequalities are precisely the Gaussian two-codeword MAC tests at receiver 1 and the single-codeword test at receiver 2; the likelihood-ratio union proof in step 1.1 with two streams proves achievability directly. The sum of the powers used is no larger than the prescribed powers, and step 2.1 selects deterministic power-feasible codebooks. This describes the changed labels and powers explicitly: all user 1 information is private at the unintended receiver, so its actual private INR can exceed the nominal $q_1$; user 2 uses only its nominal common power. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, given, construct, algebra]

5.1 If instead $r_2>A_2+E_1$, reflect the construction in step 4.1. Both extra individual inequalities cannot fail together, since that would give $S>A_1+A_2+E_1+E_2\ge E_1+E_2$, contradicting a stated sum facet. When neither fails use step 3.1. Equality cases follow by closure of these achievable regions and the power-slack limit in step 2.1. If a layer is singleton it contributes no competing index; if both rates are zero use the all-zero code. This proves the entire seven-facet region, with the explicit nominal-policy and auxiliary-removal convention in the statement. [F1, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, given, cases] ∎

**Given:** The Gaussian channel in [F1], a fixed pair of private powers, and a nonnegative rate split satisfying the strict inequalities for every nonempty decoded-stream subset with positive total rate.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the nondegenerate Gaussian-law construction.

[F1] [[def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel]]: the two receivers observe the stated linear combinations with independent unit-variance Gaussian noises and satisfy the stated power constraints.

[F2] [[cor-iid-finite-variance-weak-law]]: every IID finite-variance information-density summand obeys the weak law.

[F3] [[lem-scalar-gaussian-channel-mutual-information-power-bound]]: the scalar additive Gaussian channel mutual information equals its Gaussian variance formula for the centered Gaussian input specified here.



1.1 Generate independent message-indexed Gaussian codebooks for $U_1,V_1,U_2,V_2$, with each coordinate law matching its assigned power. The two components at transmitter $i$ sum to a Gaussian input of power $P_i$; when one component has zero power, set its rate to zero and omit it. The private component of user 2 contributes independent Gaussian noise at receiver 1, and the private component of user 1 contributes independent Gaussian noise at receiver 2, with the variances $N_1,N_2$ stated above. [A1, F1, given]

1.2 At receiver $j$, let $\mathcal D_j$ be its three decoded streams. For every nonempty $T\subseteq\mathcal D_j$, define the information density
$\imath_{j,T}(u_T;y|u_{T^c})=\ln\frac{w_j(y|u_{\mathcal D_j})}{\int w_j(y|u_T',u_{T^c})\prod_{s\in T}P_{U_s}(du_s')},$
where $w_j$ is the Gaussian output density with the other user's private stream included in its noise variance $N_j$. Decode the positive-rate streams by threshold tests for every subset with positive total rate. A zero-rate stream has a singleton message set, so it creates no competing codeword. Choose thresholds between $\ln2$ times each subset rate and its mutual information in nats. For each tested true subset, the information density is a sum of IID quadratic functions of Gaussian variables with finite variance, so [F2] makes the tests pass with probability tending to one. Condition on the complementary decoded streams and rescale the output by $N_j^{-1/2}$; [F3] and its Gaussian equality case give the stated subset mutual information in nats. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 For either receiver and any nonempty subset $T$ of incorrectly decoded streams, $T$ has positive total rate; its false codewords are independent of the output and the correctly decoded streams. The likelihood ratio for that subset has mean one under this false-candidate law, so Markov's inequality bounds the chance of passing a threshold $n\tau_T$ by $e^{-n\tau_T}$. There are at most $e^{n\ln2\sum_{s\in T}R_s+o(n)}$ false tuples. The union bound over the tested subsets tends to zero because each threshold exceeds the corresponding rate sum in nats. [F1, given, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 The ensemble error argument alone does not yet impose deterministic codebook powers. For fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$, instead generate each positive component at power $(1-\varepsilon)P_s$. The finitely many strict positive-rate subset inequalities remain valid for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, by continuity; zero-power components have zero rate and are omitted. For user $i$, let $B_{i,j}$ be the coordinate-$j$ input energy $|U_i+V_i|^2$, averaged over all of its common/private message indices, including the cross term. These variables are IID across coordinates, have mean $(1-\varepsilon)P_i$, and satisfy $\mathbb E B_{i,j}^2\le\mathbb E|U_i+V_i|^4\le3P_i^2$ by Jensen and the real Gaussian fourth moment; in the circular complex case the sharper constant is $2P_i^2$. Thus the codebook's expected average input power has variance at most $3P_i^2/n$. Chebyshev shows that the probability of either user's power exceeding its unscaled constraint tends to zero, while Markov applied to the ensemble sum of receiver errors shows that the probability of an error exceeding the square root of that ensemble mean tends to zero. Consequently some deterministic codebook simultaneously meets both power constraints and has vanishing receiver errors. If $P_i=0$, its codeword is identically zero and no concentration is needed. Taking achievable closures and then $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ recovers the stated component powers and all boundary split rates by continuity. Singleton streams create no competing codewords; if every rate is zero, use the all-zero code and obtain zero error. This proves the full real and complex fixed-split region without changing the statement. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, given, choose, algebra] ∎

**Given:** A complex Gaussian interference code with independent messages and the SNR/INR convention below; logarithms and entropies in the proof are base two.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the Gaussian-law and information suppliers.

[F1] [[def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel]]: the channel has independent unit circular Gaussian receiver noises and the stated average powers.

[F2] [[lem-it-fano-for-finite-message-density-observations]]: a vanishing-error decoder gives a message-entropy bound by mutual information plus $o(n)$.

[F3] [[lem-standard-borel-memoryless-channel-mutual-information-tensorization]]: vector mutual information on a memoryless channel is bounded by the sum of its coordinate values.

[F4] [[lem-standard-borel-conditional-mutual-information-chain-rule-and-data-processing]]: conditional chain rules and data processing identify deterministic-message and codeword information and allow revealing side information.

[F5] [[lem-scalar-gaussian-channel-mutual-information-power-bound]]: the scalar Gaussian information power bound and its equality case.

[F6] [[lem-complex-gaussian-interference-entropy-estimates]]: the entropy-difference bound and every unconditioned and genie-conditioned output entropy estimate used below, with only average power assumptions.



1.1 Write $a=\mathrm{SNR}_1$, $b=\mathrm{SNR}_2$, $c=\mathrm{INR}_1$, $d=\mathrm{INR}_2$. Give $M_2$ to receiver 1 and subtract its deterministic codeword. Fano, conditional data processing in both directions, and tensorization give $nR_1\le\sum_j I(X_{1,j};h_{11}X_{1,j}+Z_{1,j})+o(n)$. The scalar Gaussian power bound followed by Jensen and the average input constraint gives $R_1\le\log_2(1+a)$. Reflection gives $R_2\le\log_2(1+b)$. The same argument applies when a direct gain vanishes and then forces the corresponding rate to zero. Throughout the proof independent messages give independent user input vectors, regardless of coordinate dependence inside a vector; the additive Fano remainders disappear on division by $n$ and passage to the coding limit. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, given, algebra]

2.1 Reveal $X_2^n$ to receiver 1. The chain rule and independent inputs give the following exact expansion of the two augmented mutual informations: $I(X_1^n;Y_1^n|X_2^n)+I(X_2^n;Y_2^n)=h(Y_2^n)-h(Z_1^n)+h(h_{11}X_1^n+Z_1^n)-h(h_{12}X_1^n+Z_2^n)$. If $a\ge d$, the entropy-difference estimate [F6] applies with $s=|h_{11}|^2$, $t=|h_{12}|^2$, $P=P_1$; phases are removed by unit-modulus rotations. This is precisely the coupling condition $|h_{11}|\ge|h_{12}|$: the lower-SNR observation can be formed by scaling the higher-SNR observation and adding circular Gaussian noise of variance $1-t/s$. The proof of [F6] covers zero gains without division by a cross gain. Its unconditioned-output bound therefore yields $R_1+R_2\le\log_2(1+b+d)+\log_2((1+a)/(1+d))=\log_2(1+a)+\log_2(1+b/(1+d))$. Only $a\ge d$ is needed. Reflecting the argument gives the second weak sum bound under $b\ge c$, using the reflected noise coupling. [F1, F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, given, construct, algebra]

2.2 Define $S_1^n=h_{12}X_1^n+Z_2^n$ and $S_2^n=h_{21}X_2^n+Z_1^n$ using independent receiver noises. Give $S_1^n$ to receiver 1 and $S_2^n$ to receiver 2. Expanding both augmented informations gives $I(X_1^n;Y_1^n,S_1^n)+I(X_2^n;Y_2^n,S_2^n)=h(Y_1^n|S_1^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n)-h(Z_1^n)-h(Z_2^n)$: the positive $h(S_1^n)$ and $h(S_2^n)$ cancel the interference-plus-noise entropies of the two conditional channels. Applying the two conditional-output estimates in [F6] and $h(Z_i^n)=n\log_2(\pi e)$ proves the third displayed weak sum bound. This calculation is valid in every regime and requires no degradation inequality. [F1, F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, given, construct, algebra]

3.1 Add two copies of receiver 1's Fano bound and one of receiver 2's. Augment receiver 2 by $S_2^n$ and one receiver 1 copy by $X_2^n$. The resulting information sum equals $h(Y_1^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n)-2h(Z_1^n)+h(h_{11}X_1^n+Z_1^n)-h(h_{12}X_1^n+Z_2^n)$. Indeed the three information terms contribute, respectively, $h(Y_1^n)-h(S_2^n)$, $h(S_2^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n)-h(h_{12}X_1^n+Z_2^n)-h(Z_1^n)$, and $h(h_{11}X_1^n+Z_1^n)-h(Z_1^n)$. The unconditioned, conditional, and entropy-difference estimates of [F6] give $2R_1+R_2\le\log_2(1+a+c)+\log_2(1+d+b/(1+c))+\log_2((1+a)/(1+d))$. The only degradation hypothesis is $a\ge d$, exactly as in step 2.1. Reflection proves the displayed $R_1+2R_2$ bound under $b\ge c$. Thus the stated weak regime supplies every required coupling. [F1, F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, given, algebra]

3.2 In the mixed regime $c\ge b$ and $a>d$, the individual bounds and first sum bound still follow from steps 1.1–1.2. For the MAC sum bound, receiver 1 first decodes $M_1$. On the event of correct decoding it subtracts $h_{11}X_1^n$ and obtains $h_{21}X_2^n+Z_1^n$. If $h_{21}\ne0$, scale by $h_{22}/h_{21}$ and add independent circular Gaussian noise of variance $1-|h_{22}/h_{21}|^2$, which is nonnegative because $c\ge b$. Add the known vector $h_{12}X_1^n$ and apply receiver 2's decoder. Coupling this simulation to the one using the true $M_1$ bounds its joint-message error by the sum of the two original errors; a deterministic MAP decoder has no larger average error. Joint-message Fano and the unconditioned-output estimate [F6] give $R_1+R_2\le\log_2(1+a+c)$. If $h_{21}=0$, then $b=c=0$ and step 1.1 forces $R_2=0$, so the same sum bound follows immediately. This establishes the exact mixed sum claim, including degenerate gains. [F1, F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, given, construct, algebra, cases]

4.1 For the mixed weighted bound add the three Fano information terms $I(X_1^n;Y_1^n,S_1^n)$, $I(X_2^n;Y_2^n)$, and $I(X_2^n;Y_2^n,S_2^n|X_1^n)$. The first expands as $h(S_1^n)-h(Z_2^n)+h(Y_1^n|S_1^n)-h(S_2^n)$, the second as $h(Y_2^n)-h(S_1^n)$, and the third as $h(S_2^n)-h(Z_1^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n,X_1^n)-h(Z_2^n)$. Their sum is $h(Y_1^n|S_1^n)+h(Y_2^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n,X_1^n)-h(Z_1^n)-2h(Z_2^n)$. Apply the three corresponding bounds in [F6] to obtain exactly $R_1+2R_2\le\log_2(1+b+d)+\log_2(1+c+a/(1+d))+\log_2(1+b/(1+c))$. This particular weighted estimate is universal and uses no degradation condition. Reflection gives the other mixed regime. Combining the preceding steps proves every displayed inequality with precisely the hypotheses asserted in the statement. [F1, F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, given, algebra] ∎

**Given:** A complex Gaussian channel with nonnegative finite powers and the SNR/INR convention in [F2]; all logarithms in the proof are base two.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through Gaussian input and information suppliers.

[F1] [[thm-real-gaussian-strong-interference-capacity-region]]: in the strong regime, the Gaussian MAC-intersection region is exact.

[F2] [[def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel]]: $\mathrm{INR}_1$ is user 2's interference power at receiver 1 and $\mathrm{INR}_2$ is user 1's interference power at receiver 2.

[F3] [[lem-real-gaussian-han-kobayashi-inner-region]]: fixed Gaussian private/common powers achieve every feasible three-stream subset-decoding rate split, including singleton streams and closure.

[F4] [[lem-real-gaussian-interference-genie-outer-region]]: capacity obeys the displayed weak and mixed individual, sum, and weighted outer bounds.

[F5] [[lem-gaussian-superposition-nonunique-han-kobayashi-region]]: the seven Gaussian HK facets, with an explicit nine-facet elimination and auxiliary-removal construction, are achievable under the nominal split policy; its proof selects deterministic codebooks satisfying the average power constraints.



1.1 First suppose both prescribed powers are positive; zero powers are handled separately below. Write $a=\mathrm{SNR}_1$, $b=\mathrm{SNR}_2$, $c=\mathrm{INR}_1$, $d=\mathrm{INR}_2$ and $L(x)=\log_2 x$. The weak regime is $c<b$, $d<a$, the mixed regimes have exactly one reversed comparison, and the strong regime is $c\ge b$, $d\ge a$. Positive powers make these comparisons equivalent to the gain comparisons in [F1]. In the strong regime [F1] supplies the exact region, so there is no loss. We treat one mixed regime and obtain the other by exchanging all user indices. [A1, F1, F2, given, cases]

2.1 In the weak regime set $k_c=\max(1,c)$, $k_d=\max(1,d)$, $q_1=\min(1,d)$, $q_2=\min(1,c)$, $t_1=a/k_d$, $t_2=b/k_c$, $N_1=1+q_2$, and $N_2=1+q_1$. These correspond to the nominal private powers $P_{1p}=P_1/k_d$ and $P_{2p}=P_2/k_c$, including zero cross gains without division by an INR. Let $A_i,D_i,E_i,G_i$ be [F5]'s quantities for this split. Then $1\le N_i\le2$, $t_1\ge a/(1+d)$, $t_2\ge b/(1+c)$, $(N_1+t_1)(1+d)\ge1+a$, and $(N_2+t_2)(1+c)\ge1+b$: for example $(1+d)/k_d\ge1$ and $N_1\ge1$. These elementary inequalities will compare all facets uniformly, including INR below one. Denote by $O_1,O_2,O_3$ the three weak outer sum right-hand sides in their displayed order and by $W_1,W_2$ the outer $2R_1+R_2$ and $R_1+2R_2$ right-hand sides. [F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, given, choose, algebra]

2.2 In the mixed regime $c\ge b$, $d<a$, take $q_2=0$, $t_2=0$, $N_1=1$, $q_1=\min(1,d)$, $N_2=1+q_1$, $t_1=a/\max(1,d)$. Thus user 2 is nominally all common, and the private user 1 signal has unintended received power $\min(1,d)$. The seven-facet quantities become $A_1=L(1+t_1)$, $D_1=L(1+a)$, $E_1=L(1+c+t_1)$, $G_1=L(1+c+a)$, $A_2=0$, $D_2=L(1+b/N_2)$, $E_2=L((1+d)/N_2)$, and $G_2=L((1+d+b)/N_2)$. Let $O=L(1+a)+L(1+b/(1+d))$ and $V=L(1+b+d)+L(1+c+a/(1+d))+L(1+b/(1+c))$, the mixed outer first sum and weighted right sides. The remaining sum bound is $G_1$. Since $(1+d)/\max(1,d)\ge1$, we have $(1+t_1)(1+d)\ge1+a$ and $(1+c+t_1)(1+d)\ge1+c+a$. [F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, given, choose, algebra]

2.3 It remains to justify clipping a coordinate at zero; a negative-coordinate polygon argument would not do this. If both capacity coordinates are at most one, use the zero code. Suppose $R_1\le1<R_2$ and write $B=L(1+b)$. The capacity individual bound gives $R_2\le B$, so it suffices to achieve $(0,\max(0,B-1))$ on the axis. Shut user 1 off. In a weak nominal split, if $c<1$ user 2 is entirely private and achieves $B$. If $c\ge1$, its desired private power is $b/c$ and its unintended private power is one. Its common layer can be decoded at the unintended receiver while treating its private layer as noise at any rate up to $C=L((1+c)/2)$. At its intended receiver the private rate bound is $A=L(1+b/c)$, the common bound is $H=L(1+b-b/c)$, and the total bound is $B$. The product identities $(1+b/c)(1+b-b/c)\ge1+b$ and $(1+b/c)(1+c)\ge1+b$ give $A+H\ge B$ and $A+C\ge B-1$. For a total rate $T\le\min(B,A+C)$, allocate private rate $\min(A,T)$ and common rate $\max(0,T-A)$; this common rate is at most both $C$ and $H$. Every intended MAC subset inequality and the unintended common decoding inequality therefore holds, with closure for equality, so [F3] achieves at least $\max(0,B-1)$ with this same nominal split. At $c=1$ the common power and $C$ are zero and the calculation still holds. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, given, construct, algebra, cases]

3.1 The complete weak facet comparison table is $\begin{array}{c|c|c}\text{inner right side}&\text{capacity upper bound}&\text{upper bound minus inner right side}\\D_1&L(1+a)&\le L N_1\le1\\D_2&L(1+b)&\le L N_2\le1\\A_1+G_2&O_1&\le L(N_1N_2)\le2\\A_2+G_1&O_2&\le L(N_1N_2)\le2\\E_1+E_2&O_3&\le L(N_1N_2)\le2\\A_1+G_1+E_2&W_1&\le L(N_1^2N_2)\le3\\A_2+G_2+E_1&W_2&\le L(N_2^2N_1)\le3\end{array}$. Here the first two comparisons follow from $D_1=L((N_1+a)/N_1)$ and its reflection. For $A_1+G_2$, cancel the common factor $1+d+b$ in the numerator and use $(N_1+t_1)(1+d)\ge1+a$; the denominator is $N_1N_2$. The reflected inequality proves the next row. For $E_1+E_2$, each of its numerator factors $1+c+t_1$ and $1+d+t_2$ dominates the corresponding outer factor by step 2.1. For the $W_1$ row cancel $1+a+c$ and compare the remaining inner factors $(N_1+t_1)(1+d+t_2)$ with the outer factors $((1+a)/(1+d))(1+d+b/(1+c))$, factor by factor using step 2.1; the denominator is $N_1^2N_2$. Reflection gives the final row. This verifies every entry of the table by multiplication of nonnegative factors. [F4, F5, step 2.1, given, algebra]

3.2 The full mixed comparison table is $\begin{array}{c|c|c}\text{inner right side}&\text{capacity upper bound}&\text{upper bound minus inner right side}\\D_1&L(1+a)&0\\D_2&L(1+b)&\le L N_2\le1\\A_1+G_2&O&\le L N_2\le1\\A_2+G_1&G_1&0\\E_1+E_2&G_1&\le L N_2\le1\\A_1+G_1+E_2&L(1+a)+G_1&\le L N_2\le1\\A_2+G_2+E_1&V&\le L N_2+L(1+b/(1+c))\le2\end{array}$. The third row follows by canceling $1+d+b$ and using $(1+t_1)(1+d)\ge1+a$. The fifth uses $(1+c+t_1)(1+d)\ge1+c+a$. The sixth uses the former inequality after canceling $G_1$; its capacity upper bound is the sum of the individual $R_1$ bound and the MAC sum bound, hence is a valid bound on $2R_1+R_2$. In the last row $G_2$ has the same output numerator as the first term of $V$, and $1+c+t_1\ge1+c+a/(1+d)$; the sole additional outer factor is $1+b/(1+c)\le2$ because $b\le c$. These calculations prove all rows, and each gap is no larger than its facet's sum of coefficients. They include $d<1$, $d=1$, $d=0$, $b=0$, and $c=b$ directly. Therefore for mixed capacity pairs with both coordinates at least one, $(R_1-1,R_2-1)$ obeys all seven achievable facets. Reflecting indices proves the other mixed regime. [F4, F5, step 2.2, given, algebra, cases]

4.1 If a weak-regime capacity pair has $R_1,R_2\ge1$, put $r_i=R_i-1$. Subtracting one in each coordinate reduces the linear functionals with coefficient pairs $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, $(1,1)$, $(2,1)$, and $(1,2)$ by respectively $1,1,2,3,3$. The table therefore places $(r_1,r_2)$ in all seven facets of [F5], which is achievable with the nominal split and its authorized auxiliary-removal alternatives. There are no missing INR subcases: if $c<1$ then $q_2=c$ and user 2's common power is zero; if $d<1$ the reflected fact holds. The formulas remain exact, and facets made redundant by singleton streams do not need to be imposed anew. At $c=1$ or $d=1$ the formulas from the two sides coincide. If $c,d<1$, both common layers vanish and the seven-facet region reduces to the rectangle $r_1\le L(1+a/(1+c))$, $r_2\le L(1+b/(1+d))$; each individual gap is at most one. Thus the same calculation covers both sub-noise INRs, either one, and their zero and unit boundaries. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, given, algebra, cases]

5.1 For a mixed axis, the nominally all-common strongly interfering user has unintended link at least as strong as its intended link; with the other user shut off its entire intended single-user rate is decodable at both receivers. The other user's axis is covered by the calculation in step 2.3, including the entirely-private case when its INR is below one. Reflecting indices handles $R_2\le1<R_1$. Singleton layers and boundary rates follow from [F3]'s closure; the superposition and fallback regions use the explicit slack-power selection in [F5]. Thus for every weak, mixed, or strong capacity pair with positive prescribed powers there is an achievable pair whose coordinates are at least $\max(0,R_i-1)$. All changes of layer labels and powers in the non-axis seven-facet construction are exactly the permitted auxiliary removal of [F5], so the full coordinatewise claim and nominal power policy in the statement both hold. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 4.1, step 3.2, step 2.3, given, cases]

6.1 Finally let a prescribed power vanish. If $P_1=0$, the average nonnegative energy constraint forces user 1's codeword to vanish almost surely, so $R_1=0$ and $a=d=0$; the scalar individual converse gives $R_2\le L(1+b)$. If also $P_2=0$, both rates are zero. Otherwise, when $c\ge b$ the nominal all-common user 2 code achieves its exact single-user rate at both receivers, since $|h_{21}|^2P_2\ge|h_{22}|^2P_2$; there is no condition on user 1's gains to check because it sends no information. When $c<b$ the nominal private user 2 split achieves at least $\max(0,L(1+b)-1)$ by the direct axis construction of step 2.3. The case $P_2=0<P_1$ is reflected. All deterministic zero-power layers are omitted, and no argument divides by a gain or a zero power. This proves the asserted full-channel claim for nonnegative finite powers as well as the positive-power cases. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.3, step 5.1, given, cases] ∎
